source.title: Pre-training LLM without Learning Rate Decay Enhances Supervised Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Kazuki Yano; Shun Kiyono; Sosuke Kobayashi; Sho Takase; Jun Suzuki

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figure and equation formatting is garbled in the text extraction, but the reported tables and results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study does not fit scaling laws, but its own comparisons of pre-training validation loss with post-SFT performance specifically challenge the claim that downstream performance improves predictably with pre-training loss.
record.gate_note: The study varies learning-rate schedules on 1B and 8B models and reports paired pre-training and post-SFT results. It does not vary model size to test scaling, fit power laws, or test compute-optimal allocations. The schedule comparisons and sharpness measurements are reported as the study's own results; cited scaling-law results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: At fixed model size (1B, 8B), the study varies LR schedules and pairs pre- and mid-training validation loss with post-SFT task averages. The scheduler with the worst loss (WSO) gives the best SFT average in every regime. That directly tests whether downstream performance follows pre-training loss (V6, loss arm). It does not vary scale systematically or fit any law.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that WSO consistently beats decay-based schedules after SFT, across 1B/8B, mid-training and over-training, despite worse pre- or mid-training loss. They attribute this to flatter minima, and conclude that LR decay chosen to lower pre-training loss can harm downstream adaptability.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies pre-training and mid-training learning-rate schedules and evaluates post-SFT outcomes; it does not use a scaling-law fitting or extrapolation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with learning-rate scheduler and minimum learning-rate factor, stage where decay is applied, training regime, and model size. The paper also reports differing outcomes across individual downstream tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-training sharpness (Hessian trace) correlates negatively with post-SFT score across 1B schedulers (Pearson r = −0.709, 7 points). Decayed schedules reach about 2–3× higher sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-SFT downstream performance tracks loss-landscape flatness rather than pre-training loss.

record.problems: The sharpness-to-SFT correlation is reported for the 1B model and the authors note that its sample size is limited. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated comparisons. Its schedules and SFT learning-rate selection are experimental choices that limit generalization beyond the tested setups.
record.rows_left_out: None of the paired aggregate comparisons in Tables 1–4 were left out. Per-benchmark SFT results in Appendix F are not separately listed because the rows capture the reported aggregate SFT Task Avg relevant to the tested loss-to-downstream relationship.

untested.parts: No power-law fits or sweeps over parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or regimes tested for power-law form.
Predictability with scale: only two sizes, with different token budgets, and no fitted loss-to-performance function.
LR schedule changes final loss, but no exponents or compute-optimal fits are examined.

missing.what: Absolute pre-training loss vs zero-shot PT task average. These are not monotone: 1B Linear α=0 (loss 2.376) has the best avg 59.7, while the lowest-loss WSD α=0 (2.360) has 58.5. The same pattern holds at 8B and for mid-training (Table 15).
missing.locator: Table 9, Table 1 PT Task Avg column, Table 15

missing.what: Absolute loss and SFT values that allow direct loss-to-SFT ordering instead of separately referenced deltas.

record.verdict_notes: Caveats for V6. SFT LR is selected per model on AlpacaEval only. The AlpacaEval reference model is a WSO model fine-tuned at the lowest LR. No seeds or error bars are reported, and the differences are small. The over-training runs use a different batch size and token count, so they are not a clean scale comparison. This is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits or systematic sweeps over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameter and token counts.
No comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
No tests across other modalities, repeated-data regimes, or transfer settings as tests of a power-law form.
The study compares pre-training loss and downstream performance after SFT across learning-rate schedules, but does not test predictability from model scale or fit a loss-to-performance function.
No scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal fits, or fitting-choice sensitivity are examined.

relationships.condition: Fixed model size (1B and 8B), loss differences induced by the LR schedule, downstream measured after SFT; standard, mid-training and over-training regimes
relationships.reason: In all four regimes the highest-loss scheduler (WSO) gives the best SFT average, and the lowest-loss decayed runs do not (R1, R8, R15, R23, R31, R38, R3, R12, R16, R24). So loss does not predict post-SFT performance across schedules. Gaps are about 0.3–1.4 points with no uncertainty reported, hence limits rather than challenges.
relationships.display_finding: Across four regimes, WSO achieved the best fine-tuning averages despite higher validation loss than minimum-loss schedules, with gains around 0.3–1.4 points and no reported uncertainty.
